abstract: Pattern-triggered immunity (PTI) is classically associated with an extracellular respiratory burst generated by plasma membrane-localized NADPH oxidases (RBOHs). Here, we identify an ancient RBOH-independent intracellular respiratory burst driven by central carbon metabolism. Using in vivo biosensors, we demonstrate that receptor activation rapidly triggers sugar catabolism via glycolysis, shifting the NAD pool toward its reduced state. This redox pressure drives a burst in mitochondrial respiratory flux and oxygen consumption. Consequent mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (ROS) production activates ANAC017-mediated retrograde signaling to induce broader PTI gene expression. This intracellular respiratory burst represents a conserved early hallmark of immunity across land plants and links cellular carbon status to immune activation. It reveals functional parallels between plant immune metabolism and metabolic reprogramming during mammalian immune-cell activation.
